meta.scalability_note: 2 German regions (Biere, Magdeburg), managed Kubernetes (CCE), serverless functions (FunctionGraph), GPU instances, global CDN nodes
meta.performance_note: BSI C5 attested, ISO 27001 certified, 99.95% SLA for key services, Tier-4 German data centers, carrier-grade Deutsche Telekom network

AWS Amplify.note: Basic application deployment service for containerised apps; lacks full front-end hosting pipeline, CI/CD integration, and mobile backend features of AWS Amplify

AWS Lambda.note: Fully managed FaaS with Python, Node.js, Go, and Java runtimes; event-driven triggers, auto-scaling to zero, pay-per-invocation billing

Amazon ECS.equivalent: Open Telekom Cloud Cloud Container Engine (CCE)
Amazon ECS.note: Managed container service supporting Docker workloads without requiring full Kubernetes cluster management

Amazon EKS.equivalent: Open Telekom Cloud Cloud Container Engine (CCE) Kubernetes
Amazon EKS.note: Fully managed Kubernetes with automated upgrades, node pool auto-scaling, multi-AZ deployment, and integrated container registry

Amazon EC2.equivalent: Open Telekom Cloud Elastic Cloud Server (ECS)
Amazon EC2.note: Broad instance portfolio covering general purpose, compute-optimised, memory-optimised, and GPU instance families with flexible billing

AWS Batch.note: Batch workloads supported via FunctionGraph event triggers and CCE job scheduling; no dedicated managed Batch service with job queues and compute environments

AWS Elastic Beanstalk.note: No PaaS application deployment platform that automatically handles capacity provisioning, load balancing, and health monitoring

Amazon S3.equivalent: Open Telekom Cloud Object Storage Service (OBS)
Amazon S3.note: S3-compatible API with cross-region replication, versioning, lifecycle policies, server-side encryption, and fine-grained ACLs

Amazon S3 Glacier.note: Cold storage tier available within OBS as a storage class; no dedicated archival product with distinct retrieval SLA tiers (Expedited, Standard, Bulk)

Amazon EBS.equivalent: Open Telekom Cloud Elastic Volume Service (EVS)
Amazon EBS.note: High-performance SSD and Ultra-high IO persistent block volumes, detachable from instances, snapshot and backup support

AWS Backup.equivalent: Open Telekom Cloud Cloud Backup and Recovery (CBR)
AWS Backup.note: Centralised policy-based backup service covering VMs, block volumes, and databases with retention policies and cross-AZ recovery

Amazon EFS.equivalent: Open Telekom Cloud Scalable File Service (SFS)
Amazon EFS.note: Managed NFS-compatible shared file system with multi-attach support, elastic capacity scaling, and integration with ECS/CCE workloads

Amazon RDS.equivalent: Open Telekom Cloud Relational Database Service (RDS)
Amazon RDS.note: Managed MySQL, PostgreSQL, and SQL Server with automated backups, point-in-time recovery, read replicas, and automated failover

Amazon DocumentDB.equivalent: Open Telekom Cloud Document Database Service (DDS)
Amazon DocumentDB.note: Managed MongoDB-compatible document database service in general availability; comparable feature set for most use cases

Amazon DynamoDB.note: No serverless, fully managed NoSQL key-value database equivalent with single-digit millisecond latency at any scale

Amazon Timestream.note: No managed serverless time-series database service

Amazon Aurora.note: No high-performance distributed relational database engine with MySQL/PostgreSQL compatibility and multi-master replication

Amazon ElastiCache.equivalent: Open Telekom Cloud Distributed Cache Service (DCS)
Amazon ElastiCache.note: Managed Redis and Memcached with cluster mode, high availability, automatic failover, and monitoring integration

Amazon Redshift.equivalent: Open Telekom Cloud Data Warehouse Service (DWS)
Amazon Redshift.note: MPP columnar data warehouse based on GaussDB; comparable analytical workload support but less mature third-party ecosystem and tooling than Redshift

AWS Application Load Balancer.equivalent: Open Telekom Cloud Elastic Load Balancing (ELB)
AWS Application Load Balancer.note: Managed HTTP/HTTPS load balancer with TLS termination, advanced routing rules, health checks, and sticky sessions

AWS Network Load Balancer.note: TCP/UDP load balancing via the same ELB product in network mode; supports high-throughput, low-latency workloads

Amazon VPC.equivalent: Open Telekom Cloud Virtual Private Cloud
Amazon VPC.note: Full virtual networking with private networks, subnets, route tables, security groups, NAT gateways, and VPC peering

Amazon Route 53.equivalent: Open Telekom Cloud Domain Name Service (DNS)
Amazon Route 53.note: Managed DNS with full record type support, health checks, and routing policies for public and private zones

Amazon API Gateway.note: Fully managed API gateway with rate limiting, authentication (IAM, app-key), request transformation, and usage monitoring

Amazon CloudFront.equivalent: Open Telekom Cloud Content Delivery Network (CDN)
Amazon CloudFront.note: CDN service available with caching and HTTPS support; limited PoP density and edge locations compared to CloudFront's global network

AWS Direct Connect.note: Dedicated private connectivity from on-premise infrastructure to OTC, leveraging Deutsche Telekom's carrier-grade network

Amazon Rekognition.equivalent: Open Telekom Cloud Image Recognition Service
Amazon Rekognition.note: Managed image analysis service with classification and object detection; narrower feature set than Rekognition (no video analysis, face liveness, or celebrity detection)

Amazon SageMaker.note: End-to-end ML platform covering data labelling, experiment tracking, distributed training, AutoML, and model serving with endpoint management

Amazon Bedrock.note: No managed generative AI service with access to foundation models via API

AWS Glue.note: Managed data integration and ETL service; comparable for pipeline authoring but less mature than AWS Glue with a smaller connector ecosystem

Amazon EMR.note: Managed Hadoop and Spark cluster service with auto-scaling; broadly comparable to EMR for big data processing workloads

Amazon Athena.equivalent: Open Telekom Cloud Data Lake Insight (DLI)
Amazon Athena.note: Serverless SQL analytics over OBS object storage; comparable to Athena for ad-hoc querying but with a smaller SQL dialect and connector coverage

AWS IAM.equivalent: Open Telekom Cloud Identity and Access Management (IAM)
AWS IAM.note: Full RBAC with policies, federated identity via SAML 2.0 and OIDC, resource-level permissions, and multi-factor authentication

Amazon Cognito.note: No managed customer identity and access management (CIAM) service with user pools and OAuth2 flows for application authentication

AWS IAM Identity Center.note: No centralised single sign-on service for managing access across multiple OTC accounts or third-party SaaS applications

AWS KMS.equivalent: Open Telekom Cloud Data Encryption Workshop (DEW)
AWS KMS.note: Managed key lifecycle management with HSM-backed key storage, BYOK support, and integration with OBS, EVS, RDS, and other services

AWS Secrets Manager.equivalent: Open Telekom Cloud Cloud Secret Manager
AWS Secrets Manager.note: Managed secrets storage in general availability; limited automated rotation support compared to AWS Secrets Manager

AWS Certificate Manager.equivalent: Open Telekom Cloud SSL Certificate Manager (SCM)
AWS Certificate Manager.note: Managed TLS certificate provisioning, renewal, and deployment to ELB and CDN endpoints

Amazon GuardDuty.equivalent: Open Telekom Cloud Host Security Service (HSS)
Amazon GuardDuty.note: Workload-level threat detection covering vulnerability scanning, intrusion detection, and file integrity monitoring; less comprehensive than GuardDuty's network and API behaviour analysis

AWS Security Hub.note: Centralised security posture overview and compliance reporting; fewer automated remediations and integrated findings standards than AWS Security Hub

AWS Config.note: Resource configuration compliance and change tracking service; limited managed rule library and fewer integration points than AWS Config

AWS Shield.note: Managed DDoS protection at both network and application layers with real-time traffic scrubbing and attack reporting

AWS WAF.equivalent: Open Telekom Cloud Web Application Firewall (WAF)
AWS WAF.note: Managed WAF with OWASP rule sets, custom rule policies, rate limiting, and bot mitigation integrated with ELB and CDN

AWS CloudTrail.equivalent: Open Telekom Cloud Cloud Trace Service (CTS)
AWS CloudTrail.note: Full API audit trail with real-time log streaming to LTS, long-term retention, and integration with Cloud Eye alerts and SMN notifications

Amazon CloudWatch.note: Metrics collection, custom dashboards, threshold alarms, and auto-scaling triggers across compute, storage, and networking resources; broadly comparable to CloudWatch

Amazon SNS.equivalent: Open Telekom Cloud Simple Message Notification (SMN)
Amazon SNS.note: Managed pub/sub service with delivery to email, SMS, HTTP/HTTPS endpoints, and FunctionGraph triggers

AWS Systems Manager.equivalent: Open Telekom Cloud Operational Management Center (OMC)
AWS Systems Manager.note: Basic infrastructure operations and resource management; lacks the breadth of Systems Manager capabilities such as Session Manager, Patch Manager, and Parameter Store

AWS Cost Explorer.note: Detailed cost breakdown by resource, project, and time period with budget alerts and cost forecasting

AWS CodeBuild.note: Managed CI build service as part of the CodeArts DevOps suite; comparable for standard build pipelines but tighter ecosystem lock-in

AWS CodeDeploy.note: Managed deployment automation supporting rolling and blue-green deployment strategies; part of the integrated CodeArts suite

AWS CodePipeline.note: Managed CI/CD pipeline orchestration with stage-gate controls and approval actions; broadly comparable to CodePipeline within the OTC ecosystem

Amazon ECR.equivalent: Open Telekom Cloud SoftWare Repository for Container (SWR)
Amazon ECR.note: Managed container registry with image vulnerability scanning, fine-grained access control, and deep integration with CCE Kubernetes

AWS CloudFormation.equivalent: Open Telekom Cloud Resource Formation Service (RFS)
AWS CloudFormation.note: IaC service with OTC-native template language for declarative resource provisioning; official Terraform provider also available for multi-cloud workflows

AWS IoT Core.equivalent: Open Telekom Cloud IoT Device Access (IoTDA)
AWS IoT Core.note: Managed MQTT and HTTPS broker with device shadow, rule engine for event-driven processing, and integration with other OTC services

AWS IoT Device Management.equivalent: Open Telekom Cloud IoT Device Management
AWS IoT Device Management.note: Device registry, OTA firmware and software update management, device grouping, and fleet monitoring dashboard

Amazon SQS.equivalent: Open Telekom Cloud Distributed Message Service (DMS) — RocketMQ/Kafka
Amazon SQS.note: Managed message queuing with RocketMQ supporting SQS-compatible point-to-point semantics, dead-letter queues, and message retention

Amazon EventBridge.note: Basic event routing service for cloud resource events; limited custom rule engine and fewer event source integrations compared to EventBridge

AWS Step Functions.note: No managed serverless workflow orchestration or state machine service

Amazon SES.equivalent: Open Telekom Cloud Simple Message Notification (email)
Amazon SES.note: Email notifications available via SMN; no dedicated high-volume transactional email service with deliverability analytics, DKIM/DMARC management, or suppression lists

Amazon Kinesis.note: Managed Apache Kafka service supporting real-time data streaming and event streaming pipelines; comparable to Kinesis Data Streams for high-throughput ingestion
